projections.scenario: Furthest published year. IEA Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2025, today's policy settings. METRIC DIFFERS: average share of the TOP THREE refining countries, not the single top country.
projections.source: IEA GCMO 2025, via Hydrocarbon Processing (21 May 2025); 2020 = ~82%, 2024 = 86% via Mining Technology
projections.note: Not directly comparable with the factor (top-one average, 72% in 2025). No 2035 top-one average from the 2026 edition was found in readable coverage.

projections.scenario: Furthest published year. IEA GCMO 2026, if planned projects proceed on schedule. RARE EARTHS ONLY.
projections.source: IEA GCMO 2026 press release, via Global Mining Review (17 Jul 2026)
projections.note: Top supplier's share of rare-earth refining: over 90% in 2023, 85% in 2025. Rare earths are excluded from the factor's 72% average.

projections.scenario: Furthest published year. IEA GCMO 2026, current policy settings, announced project pipeline.
projections.source: IEA GCMO 2026, via ANI/Times of Oman (27 Jul 2026)
projections.note: Primary copper supply shortfall as a share of demand. Narrowed as DRC and Zambia projects advanced (ANI via The Tribune).

projections.scenario: IEA GCMO 2025, current government policies (previous edition).
projections.source: IEA GCMO 2025, via Global Trade Review (21 May 2025)
projections.note: Superseded by the 2026 edition (25%). Kept for the trend.

projections.scenario: IEA GCMO 2025, Net Zero Emissions by 2050 scenario.
projections.source: IEA GCMO 2025, via Global Trade Review (21 May 2025)
projections.note: Higher demand pathway; the 2026 edition's net-zero gap was not found in readable coverage.

No published module-price ($/W) projection to 2050 or 2100 found. Related: DNV (ETO, Oct 2023, via PV Tech) projects solar LCOE falling from ~US$41/MWh to US$21/MWh by 2050, learning rate 26% falling to 17%: different unit, do not plot on the $/W axis.

projections.scenario: BNEF near-term outlook from the December 2025 battery price survey.
projections.note: About 3% below 2025's $108/kWh. BNEF's own page confirms only that prices are expected to fall again in 2026.

projections.scenario: Furthest published year. BNEF outlook from the December 2024 survey (older vintage).
projections.note: That vintage also expected sub-$100/kWh in 2026, which the Dec 2025 survey pushed back ($105 expected for 2026). The 2023 survey expected $80/kWh in 2030 (BNEF press release, Nov 2023). The Dec 2025 long-term forecast is paywalled.

No published projection of the clean share. The IEA Net Zero Roadmap (2023, via The National) requires ~$4.5 trillion/yr clean investment by the early 2030s (vs $1.8T in 2023); with fossil held at 2026's $1.2T that implies ~79% clean (derived, not a forecast).

thresholds.label: One country half
thresholds.consequence: One government can trigger a global shortage of a key mineral.

thresholds.label: Near-monopoly
thresholds.consequence: Alternatives barely exist; export controls can halt factories abroad within months.
thresholds.source: Judgment; benchmark is rare-earth refining at 85% in 2025 (IEA GCMO 2026), when April 2025 controls forced automaker cuts

thresholds.label: IEA 2025 gap
thresholds.consequence: Sustained copper price spikes; grid and EV build-out delayed.
thresholds.source: Judgment, set at the IEA GCMO 2025 stated-policies projection

thresholds.label: Net-zero gap
thresholds.consequence: Copper, not policy, caps how fast the world can electrify.
thresholds.source: Judgment, set at the IEA GCMO 2025 net-zero-scenario gap

thresholds.label: Price reversal
thresholds.consequence: Near doubling of module prices; signals supply shock or trade split.

thresholds.label: Supply shock
thresholds.consequence: Solar loses much of its cost edge; electrification slows.

thresholds.label: EV parity
thresholds.consequence: Above it, electric cars cost more upfront than petrol cars.
thresholds.source: BloombergNEF benchmark for upfront price parity with gasoline cars, via Bloomberg/Transport Topics (Dec 2024)

thresholds.label: 2022 spike
thresholds.consequence: Back to 2022 prices; storage and EV adoption stall.
thresholds.source: Judgment; BNEF average was $151/kWh in 2022, its first-ever rise (via The Driven, Nov 2023)

thresholds.label: 1.5°C pace
thresholds.consequence: Below it, investment falls short of the IEA net-zero requirement.
thresholds.source: Derived by this site: IEA Net Zero Roadmap 2023 ($4.5T/yr clean by early 2030s) with fossil held at $1.2T

thresholds.label: Parity 1:1
thresholds.consequence: Fossil spending matches clean again, as around 2018; transition stalls.
thresholds.source: Judgment; 1:1 ratio around 2018 per IEA WEI 2023, via pv magazine

exceedance.reasoning: Already crossed (72%), so this is the chance it is still above 50% in 2100: the IEA sees only marginal easing by 2035, but 75 years of diversification, recycling and substitution make a fall below half more likely than not.

Chance the average reaches 85% in any year before 2100: it is rising about a point a year (70% to 72%, 2023-2025), but rare-earth refining is already diversifying and rich-country public finance quadrupled to $65 billion.

Chance that a projected ten-year-ahead shortfall of 30% or more recurs before 2100: grades are falling and mines take over 16 years, but the gap narrowed from 30% to 25% in a year and high prices drive recycling and aluminium substitution.
A 40% gap needs net-zero-pace demand with today's supply pipeline; demand that fast is itself uncertain and would raise prices enough to pull in new supply and substitutes.

exceedance.source: Judgment informed by InfoLink, ITRPV 2026, Caixin
exceedance.reasoning: Chance the real global benchmark price exceeds $0.20/W in any year before 2100: a 26% learning rate and huge overcapacity push prices down, but today's prices are below cost and a China supply or trade shock could double them for a time.

A fourfold real rise would need a prolonged collapse of the dominant supply chain or a major war; regional prices (US $0.31/W) show trade barriers raise local prices without moving the global benchmark that far.
Already above (108), so this is the chance the real average is still above $100/kWh in 2100: storage packs are at $70 and LFP at $81 already, and BNEF expects further falls.

exceedance.source: Judgment informed by BNEF 2022 price rise
exceedance.reasoning: Chance the real average tops $150/kWh in any year before 2100: it happened once (2022, $151) during a metals spike, but in 2025 a 124% metal-price jump still left pack prices falling.

exceedance.source: Judgment informed by IEA WEI 2026 and Net Zero Roadmap 2023
exceedance.reasoning: Already below (65%), so this is the chance the share is still below 79% in 2100: by then most fossil supply investment should have shrunk under almost any cost trend, though gas and coal investment are rising in 2026.

exceedance.source: Judgment informed by IEA WEI 2023 and 2026
exceedance.reasoning: Chance the clean share falls back below parity in any year before 2100: clean costs keep falling, but a fossil price spike or a security-driven drilling boom could briefly flip the ratio, as gas and coal investment are at multi-year highs.

notes: iea.org is blocked to automated fetching (Cloudflare 403). Every IEA number here was read in named secondary coverage (ANI/Tribune/Times of Oman, Anadolu, Global Mining Review, BOFIT, Hydrocarbon Processing, Mining Technology, GTR, Down To Earth, The National, pv magazine). Worth a manual check against the IEA reports.

mineral_concentration: the 72% (2025, from 70% in 2023) excludes rare earths. ANI words it as the 'top refining country' average; Anadolu says 'the average share held by China'. They are equivalent only where China is the top refiner (Indonesia leads nickel). The site's 'top refining country' wording matches ANI.

mineral_concentration: the 2025 IEA edition used a different metric, the top-three average (82% in 2020, 86% in 2024, projected 82% in 2035). Do not mix it with the top-one 72%. No 2035/2040 top-one projection from the 2026 edition was found in readable coverage.

mineral_concentration: China's refining shares per IEA GCMO 2026 (via BOFIT, 7 Aug 2026): battery-grade graphite 94%, cobalt 76%, lithium 74%, magnet rare earths 84%, copper 47%, nickel 31%. Anadolu gives rare earths at 85% (top supplier, 2025); BOFIT gives 84% for magnet REEs. The definitions may differ slightly.

Export controls status (24 Nov 2026): China suspended its October 2025 expanded rare-earth controls for a year, and on 9 Nov 2026 extended the pause to 10 Jan 2027 (The National). The April 2025 controls on seven heavy rare earths appear still in force (search snippets of S&P Global; not read directly).

copper_gap: lead time. I verified 'more than 16 years' on average from discovery to first production (IEA 2021, mines opened 2010-2019, via Industrial Info Resources, 5 May 2021). The exact '16.5 years' appears only in a 403-blocked Mining News page, so it is unverified. Note that factors.ts siNote says 'about 17 years'. Suggest 'more than 16 years'.

copper_gap: the 25% (2026 edition) is primary copper supply vs demand under current policy settings. The 2025 edition gave 30% (current policies) and 40% (net zero). Copper investment rose 8% in 2025 (Anadolu).

solar_price: the InfoLink USD TOPCon row (18 Nov 2026) shows avg 0.114, low 0.100 and an implausible high of 0.500, likely an outlier in a single quote. ITRPV gives about US$0.09/Wp at end-2025 on a different basis. The ITRPV learning rate is 26% (1976-2025), up from 24.9% in the 15th edition. Fraunhofer ISE's 25.7% was seen only in a search snippet, not read.

solar_price: no published $/W projection to 2050/2100 was found. Chinese makers sold below cost in 2026 (polysilicon down 40%+ year-to-date by late July, utilisation 40-60%, Caixin). SAMR price-compliance push from 31 Jul 2026 with no numeric floor (pv magazine USA). Reported RMB 0.79/W TOPCon floor talks (TaiyangNews) were not read and remain unconfirmed.

battery_price: BNEF says 2025's $108 is 8% below 2024. The 2024 survey reported $115, which looks like a 6% fall; the gap is presumably BNEF restating 2024 in real 2025 dollars (not confirmed on the page). The 2010 starting value is $1,436/kWh (Canary Media, Dec 2024), while earlier BNEF editions quoted about $1,100-1,200, so the dollar basis differs by edition.

clean_investment: 64.7% = 2.2/(2.2+1.2) using rounded IEA figures; the IEA's own unrounded share may differ by about a point. The 2024 edition's 'almost two dollars clean per fossil dollar' was seen only in search snippets, and 2026's ~1.8:1 suggests a slight dip since then.

Exceedance convention used here: for thresholds already crossed today (minerals 50%, battery $100, clean 79%), the probability is that the value is still beyond the line in 2100. For thresholds not yet crossed, it is the probability of crossing in at least one year before 2100 (annual average, real dollars for prices). All are judged; nothing published gives these probabilities.
